**The ontology reveals a tightly coupled network where eleven business entities span the physical mine through to revenue, with 18 links that trace cause and effect from equipment failure to financial outcome—built almost entirely on real SAP master data.**

What stands out is the **"golden thread" from event to P&L**: a ship-loader outage (FLEET_ASSET) delays a vessel call (VESSEL_CALL), which defers revenue (QUARTER), while the root cause—a critical spare (MATERIAL) from a single supplier (SUPPLIER)—shows up as both maintenance cost (COST_ELEMENT) and lost margin. Four of the five hard questions walk this chain, and every link is answerable because the ontology conforms operational telemetry (OPS provenance) to SAP keys—Plant, Equipment, Material, MaintenanceNotification—allowing breakdowns to be joined to P&L in one query.

The weakness is **Customer and BillingDocument**, which carry SAP_STANDIN provenance: vessel sales are approximated, not pulled from live billing. This limits margin analysis and sales-contract tie-out.

| Entity / Link | Provenance | Semantic Tables | Key Gap |
|---------------|------------|-----------------|---------|
| Site, Material, Supplier, Notification, Cost Element, Project, Workforce | **SAP** | 27 tables | None |
| Fleet Asset, Vessel Call | **MIXED** (SAP + OPS) | 15 tables | None |
| Customer | **SAP_STANDIN** | 1 table | No real billing link |
| 18 links | **MIXED** (join keys span SAP & OPS) | All questions answerable | Customer revenue not auditable |

**Next step:** Replace the stand-in Customer and BillingDocument entities with live SAP S/4 SD billing documents and payer records to close the revenue loop and enable contract-price variance analysis.

---

**Sources**  
*SAP:* SITE, NOTIFICATION, MATERIAL, SUPPLIER, COST_ELEMENT, PROJECT, PERSON  
*MIXED (SAP + OPS):* FLEET_ASSET, VESSEL_CALL, all 18 links  
*SAP_STANDIN:* CUSTOMER  
*Note: data is simulated for a fictional operator.*
